nodes.name: Colloidal Synthesis of Co-TiO2 Nanobipyramids
nodes.procedure: Synthesis of Co-doped anatase TiO2 nanobipyramids using mixed Co and Ti precursors (TiCl4 to TiF4 ratio of 4:1) in a solution containing ODE, OAc, and OAm. Water released from surfactants at elevated temperatures drives hydrolysis.

unit_operations.name: Thermal decomposition and hydrolysis
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: thermal decomposition of Co and Ti precursors in a solution containing 1-octadecene (ODE), oleic acid (OAc), and oleylamine (OAm)... hydrolysis of the Ti precursor occurred when small quantities of water released from OAm and OAc at elevated temperatures

nodes.source_text: The shape-controlled synthesis of Co-TiO2 anatase-phase nanocrystals was conducted using a colloidal method that involved the thermal decomposition of Co and Ti precursors ... Specifically, a TiCl4 to TiF4 ratio of 4:1 led to the creation of TiO2 nanobipyramids

nodes.source_text: The overpotential required to achieve current densities of 10 mA cm-2 and 100 mA cm-2 for Co-TiO2 nanoplates was measured at 370 mV and 430 mV... The Co-TiO2 nanoplates exhibited TOFs of 12.1 s-1 at 300 mV, 58.0 s-1 at 350 mV, and 385.6 s-1 at 400 mV overpotential... Tafel slopes are determined to be 62 mV dec-1... FEs for O2 formation... exceeded 98%.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show bipyramidal morphology (17.0 nm length) and nanoplate morphology (5.8 nm thickness) for Co-TiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1B, S2 shows the bipyramidal morphology of Co-TiO2, with a length of 17.0 ± 2.0 nm and a width of 9.3 ± 0.8 nm, and Figure 1F, S3 depicts the morphology of Co-TiO2 nanoplates, with dimensions of 5.8 ± 0.5 nm in length (thickness) and 16.7 ± 1.5 nm in width.

properties.observation: Shows a crystalline nanoparticle with visible lattice fringes, indicating a well-ordered atomic structure. The particle exhibits a somewhat irregular or possibly coated surface.

properties.description: An HRTEM image displaying clear, parallel lattice fringes within a distinct crystalline domain, indicative of a well-ordered atomic structure at the nanoscale.
Microscopic image showing the morphology, size, and distribution of nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM analysis confirms the single-crystal structure of nanobipyramids with side {101} facets and top/bottom {001} facets, and nanoplates with predominant {001} surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM analysis of Co-TiO2 nanobipyramids reveals a characteristic single crystal structure, displaying the {101} surfaces on the side planes and the {001} surfaces on the top and bottom (Figure 1C). Meanwhile, the nanoplates exhibit a predominant {001} surface complemented by the {101} side facets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy verified the variation in surface exposure of {001} and {101} facets based on Eg and Alg peak intensities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy (Figure S4) was employed to verify the variation in surface exposure ratios of the {001} and {101} facets. A higher exposure of the {001} facet is evidenced by a decrease in the Eg peak intensity and an increase in the Alg peak intensity

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirmed the anatase phase (JCPDS No. 02-0387) for both TiO2 and Co-TiO2, indicating Co doping does not alter the phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns, shown in Figure 2A and S5, confirm the anatase phase of TiO2 in the as synthesized nanocrystals ... incorporation of Co dopant does not introduce any new diffraction peaks

properties.purpose: Crystallographic analysis, phase identification, lattice parameter determination.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge EXAFS confirms single-site Co substitution in the TiO2 matrix; ex-situ post-OER analysis confirms the single-site coordination remained stable.
nodes.evidence_snippet: cobalt dopants are atomically dispersed single sites, homogeneously integrated into the TiO2 matrix ... Ex-situ EXAFS analysis of the Co-TiO2 nanocrystals ... confirmed that the chemical environment of the single-site Co remained stable after the OER tests.

properties.description: Comparison of Fourier-transformed EXAFS spectra for various cobalt-containing materials and reference compounds, likely measured at the Co K-edge.
Comparison of EXAFS Fourier Transforms for Co-TiO₂ nanobipyramids and nanoplates, before and after electrochemical treatment (EC).

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV in 1M KOH showed the nanoplates require overpotentials of 370 mV and 430 mV for 10 and 100 mA/cm2, outperforming nanobipyramids.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), depicted in Figure 3A and S10, demonstrates that the Co-TiO2 nanocrystals exhibit significantly higher OER activity ... overpotential required to achieve current densities of 10 mA cm-2Geo and 100 mA cm-2Geo for Co-TiO2 nanoplates was measured at 370 mV and 430 mV

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was used to determine the Electrochemical Active Surface Area (ECSA).
nodes.evidence_snippet: electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) of both the Co-TiO2 nanoplate and nanobipyramid electrodes was calculated from measurements of the electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Figure S21, S22).

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy quantified the Co doping levels at 3.9% for nanobipyramids and 3.5% for nanoplates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: concentrations quantified using energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Figure S6) ... controlled Co dopant concentration to be 3.9% for nanobipyramids and 3.5% for nanoplates.

nodes.characterization_summary: Online gas chromatography (GC) demonstrated Faradaic efficiencies for O2 formation exceeding 98% for nanoplates and 92% for nanobipyramids at 100 mA/cm2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Faradaic efficiency (FE) analyses ... conducted using online gas chromatography (GC) ... FEs for O2 formation using the Co-TiO2 nanoplate catalyst exceeded 98% ... nanobipyramid catalyst ... displayed a slightly lower FE of 92% at 100 mA cm-2.

properties.data_summary: This bar chart compares the Faradaic Efficiency of Co-TiO₂ nanoplates and Co-TiO₂ nanobipyramids at three different current densities (10, 50, and 100 mA cm⁻²). The Co-TiO₂ nanoplates consistently exhibit higher Faradaic Efficiency (approximately 98-99%) across all tested current densities compared to the Co-TiO₂ nanobipyramids (approximately 90-95%).

nodes.characterization_summary: Chronoamperometric tests confirmed the stability of the Co-TiO2 nanoplates, showing only minor decay at high current densities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Chronoamperometric (CA) tests (Figure S23) confirmed the robust stability of the Co-TiO2 nanoplate catalyst, although there was a minor decay observed at higher current densities.

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) confirmed the single-crystalline nature of individual nanobipyramids and nanoplates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image of Co-TiO2 nanobipyramids (inset shows the SAED pattern of a single nanobipyramids) ... (inset shows the SAED pattern of a single nanoplate)

nodes.characterization_summary: Electron energy loss spectroscopy mapping confirms the uniform, homogeneous distribution of Co and Ti dopants across the nanocrystal morphologies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform distribution of Co dopants across both morphologies has been verified through electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) and elemental mapping (nanobipyramids in Figure 1D, 1E; nanoplates in Figure 1H, 1I).
